title: Simple Harmonic Motion: The Physics of Oscillation

questions.question: The defining condition for simple harmonic motion is that the restoring force is:
options: Proportional to displacement and directed towards the mean position
Proportional to the square of displacement
Always directed away from the mean position
questions.rationale: SHM requires F = −kx: force proportional to displacement, acting back towards the equilibrium (mean) position.

questions.question: Where is a body in SHM moving fastest?
options: It moves at constant speed everywhere
questions.rationale: All the energy is kinetic at the mean position, so speed is maximum there, and momentarily zero at the extremes.

questions.question: The period of a mass–spring oscillator depends on:
questions.rationale: T = 2π√(m/k) involves only the mass and the spring stiffness — not the amplitude of oscillation.

questions.question: A simple pendulum's period on Earth is 2 s. Taken to the Moon where g is about one-sixth, its period becomes roughly:
questions.rationale: T ∝ 1/√g. Reducing g by a factor of 6 increases T by √6 ≈ 2.45, so 2 s becomes about 4.9 s ≈ 5 s.

questions.question: Doubling the length of a simple pendulum changes its period by a factor of:
questions.rationale: T = 2π√(l/g), so T scales with the square root of length: doubling l multiplies T by √2.

questions.question: The total energy of a spring–mass system in SHM equals:
questions.rationale: Total energy E = ½kA², set by the amplitude; it converts fully between kinetic and potential forms during the motion.

questions.question: Resonance occurs when:
options: The driving frequency matches the system's natural frequency
questions.rationale: Driving an oscillator at its natural frequency feeds energy in step with the motion, so the amplitude grows dramatically — resonance.

questions.question: Why do soldiers break step while marching across a bridge?
options: To avoid setting up forced oscillations at the bridge's natural frequency
questions.rationale: Rhythmic marching could match the bridge's natural frequency and excite destructive resonance, as famously happened at Angers Bridge (1850).

questions.question: Damping in an oscillating system:
questions.rationale: Damping (friction, air resistance) drains energy each cycle, so the amplitude decays over time while the system settles towards equilibrium.

questions.question: Radio receivers select one station among many broadcasting simultaneously by using:
options: Resonance — tuning the circuit to one frequency
questions.rationale: The tuner adjusts the circuit's natural frequency until it resonates with one station's carrier wave, amplifying only that signal.
